name: Tali Sree Mahadeva Kshetram, Angadippuram
tagline: Ancient Tali Shiva kshetram of Angadippuram with a living prasna (astrological) tradition
summary: Ancient Shiva kshetram in Angadippuram, Malappuram, known locally as the Tali Temple; it retains a living tradition of temple astrological rites (Ashtamangala/Devaprasna) and periodic yajñas.
description: Tali Sree Mahadeva Kshetram is an ancient Shiva temple in the temple-town of Angadippuram (Perinthalmanna area). The shrine forms part of the local network of historic Tali temples and is listed by Kerala tourism as a heritage temple of the area. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/thali-temple-malappuram/518/?utm_source=openai))

The temple matters to devotees for its Siva worship and to the local community as a centre for ritual decision-making: local records and temple tradition record performance of Ashtamangala/Devaprasna (ritual-prasna) inquiries and related tantric prescriptions in the recent past, and the kshetram continues to host large yajñas and ritual programmes. ([kalyangeetha.wordpress.com](https://kalyangeetha.wordpress.com/category/kshethradanam-temple-tours/kerala-temples/?utm_source=openai))

Visitors find a compact historic complex near the better-known Thirumandhamkunnu shrine in Angadippuram — the experience combines devotional darshan, periodic fire-yajñas and the visible presence of temple thanthric and astrological practice. For folklore and origin stories (Parasurama associations, local legends) treat them as tradition rather than historical fact. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angadipuram?utm_source=openai))

Practical arrangements and festival calendars are managed by the temple; the kshetram’s official pages list the head priest and public ritual programmes (including major yagnas). Confirm specific puja times, prasna events or bookings with the temple before travel. ([sreetalimahadevakshetram.in](https://sreetalimahadevakshetram.in/?utm_source=openai))
highlights: Ancient Shiva shrine in Angadippuram temple town (near Thirumandhamkunnu).
Living tradition of Ashtamangala / Devaprasna (temple horary-astrology) used for ritual decisions.
Hosts large yajñas and special abhishekams; temple published Aagneyam 2026 programme.
Managed local ritual life with a named head priest and active festival calendar. ([sreetalimahadevakshetram.in](https://sreetalimahadevakshetram.in/?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Background
body: Tali Sree Mahadeva Kshetram is one of the historic Shaiva shrines of the Valluvanad/Angadippuram area. Local tradition connects it with the class of 'Tali' Shiva temples found across Kerala; these associations are part of the temple’s living identity. ([keralawindow.net](https://keralawindow.net/templesofmalappuram.html?utm_source=openai))

Historically the temple has been an active centre for ritual consultations. In Kerala temple culture, Ashtamangala/Devaprasna (ritual-prasna) is the formal astrological reading used to determine the deity’s will; local reports and temple accounts record such prasna rites at Angadippuram in recent decades. Treat these reports as temple tradition and contemporary practice rather than archaeological fact. ([kalyangeetha.wordpress.com](https://kalyangeetha.wordpress.com/category/kshethradanam-temple-tours/kerala-temples/?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Darshan and daily poojas: visit during morning and evening puja hours for darshan of the Shiva lingam and to observe routine thanthric worship. The temple’s public pages list morning abhishekam and other regular ceremonies. ([sreetalimahadevakshetram.in](https://sreetalimahadevakshetram.in/?utm_source=openai))

Observe ritual life: when large rites are held (yajñas, kalasams, or the Aagneyam programme recorded for 2026) you can see collective ritual action, priests (thanthris) and specialist astrologers at work. If an Ashtamangala or Devaprasna is scheduled, it will be conducted by appointed pandits and follow Kerala’s prasna procedures. ([sreetalimahadevakshetram.in](https://sreetalimahadevakshetram.in/aagneyam-2026/?utm_source=openai))

Combine with nearby shrines: Angadippuram is a compact temple town; combine a visit to the Tali with the Thirumandhamkunnu Bhagavathy Temple and other local kshetrams for a fuller sense of the region’s ritual calendar. ([tourism.nammudekeralam.com](https://tourism.nammudekeralam.com/destination/thirumandhamkunnu-bhagavathy-temple/?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Location and access: the temple stands in Angadippuram, near Perinthalmanna (the temple is commonly described as about 3 km from Perinthalmanna). Arrive by road; the Angadippuram railway station on the Shoranur–Nilambur line is the nearest railhead. Confirm darshan and puja timings with the temple before you travel. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/thali-temple-malappuram/518/?utm_source=openai))

Participation and observation: if you hope to observe or participate in prasna/astrological ceremonies, contact the temple office in advance — many prasna rituals are formal, invite-only or require prior arrangements. The temple website lists contact routes and special pooja booking options. ([sreetalimahadevakshetram.in](https://sreetalimahadevakshetram.in/?utm_source=openai))
Respect and conduct: follow temple dress and conduct norms, respect priestly space during thanthric rites, and ask permission before photographing ritual acts or priests.

latest.text: Temple published and conducted a major ritual programme (Aagneyam) with multi-day yajña activities listed for April 30–May 3, 2026 on the temple site.

visitorInfo.howToReach: By road from Perinthalmanna (about 3 km); nearest railway station Angadippuram on the Shoranur–Nilambur line; reachable from Malappuram and Perinthalmanna by local buses or taxi. Confirm schedules before travel. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/destination/thali-temple-malappuram/518/?utm_source=openai))
etiquette: If you want to observe or request a prasna (devaprasnam/ashtamangala), contact the temple trustees in advance — these rites are formal and scheduled.
Follow standard temple etiquette: modest dress, remove footwear, and ask before photographing priests or rituals.

Confirm puja timings and special-event closures with the temple; the temple site lists booking/contact details but always re-check before travel. ([sreetalimahadevakshetram.in](https://sreetalimahadevakshetram.in/?utm_source=openai))
